subject: Marketplace listing lift-and-fallback: SKU prioritization per cloud
messages:
From: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aws-partner.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: rafael.gomez@azure-marketplace.com; priya.shah@gcp-partner.org
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood listing — initial SKU + region asks

Hi Sofia — great to meet at the partner summit last week. AWS marketplace onboarding team here — we want to align on a lean listing approach so customers can buy Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private through our co-sell channels. A few concrete asks to start the project: 

1) A primary SKU you want to list per cloud (we recommend 1-2 SKUs at launch).
2) Region availability matrix by cloud (which regions you can support day-one and which are tactical fallbacks).
3) Any canary/alpha packaging you want hidden behind early access.

If you can send a one-page SKU map + preferred fallback rules by EOD Monday, we’ll scope the integration and co-sell enablement timeline. Attaching the AWS listing checklist as a reference.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Dubois | AWS Marketplace Partner Solutions
Attachment: aws-listing-checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aws-partner.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood listing — initial SKU + region asks

Hi Claire — thanks, and glad we connected. Quick response while we gather the SKU map:

• We’ll propose 3 named SKUs for vendor-neutral coverage: Hosted-API, Dedicated-1 (reserved GPU pool), Private-VPC.
• Day-one regions (US-first): us-east-1, us-west-2 on AWS; East US, West US on Azure; us-central1 on GCP.
• Fallback policy: prefer same-cloud region fallback first, then cross-cloud routed to Hosted-API variant with prefix caching enabled for latency-sensitive calls.

I’m looping in Marissa and Ben to finalize real SKU IDs, pricing tiers, and the canary packaging options — we’ll get the CSV over by Monday.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Head, Cloud GTM — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -0800
Subject: SKU map draft + canary ideas (internal)

Team — draft below; I’ll attach a CSV and playbook PDF in the external reply. Please review and flag any hard constraints.

SKU naming (proposal):
- RW-API-STD — Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) — public list
- RW-DED-BASE — Dedicated (monthly reserved) — listed with quota limits and co-sell price bands
- RW-PRIV-VPC — Private (VPC/on-prem) — listed but marked enterprise-approval required (manual procurement)

Region plan (per cloud):
AWS: day-one us-east-1, us-west-2; fallback eu-west-1 for cross-region failover (limited capacity)
Azure: East US, West US; fallback North Europe for EU customers
GCP: us-central1; fallback us-west1 and europe-west3 for expansion

Canary packaging:
- Hidden SKU: RW-API-CANARY limited to 10 customers via marketplace private offers. Enable streaming + experimental quantization profiles.
- Canary fallback: if RW-DED-BASE capacity full, route to RW-API-CANARY for early customers with 95th-pct latency warnings.

Pricing bands (high level):
- API STD: per token pricing, public
- DED BASE: committed monthly price with a co-sell discount tier (to be negotiated)
- PRIV VPC: MSRP + onboarding fee (sales-assisted)

Open questions: 1) Do we want the Private SKU universally visible or gated behind an approval form? 2) Which clouds require dedicated listing IDs vs. a single multi-cloud listing?

—Marissa
Attachment: redwood_marketplace_sku_map_v1.csv (internal draft)

From: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aws-partner.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood listing — initial SKU + region asks

Thanks, Sofia and Marissa — this is helpful. A few notes from AWS listing ops: 

• Hidden canary SKU is supported via Private Offers — include a customer allowlist and we can set a soft quota.
• Private/VPC SKU needs a separate procurement workflow entry; recommend gating via an approval form on the listing with a contact email (we’ll accept a dedicated support alias).
• For fallback routing: AWS recommends prioritizing intra-cloud fallback (same cloud different region) unless the customer explicitly buys cross-cloud transit. We can support an automated redirect to a Hosted-API contract for short-term failures, but the customer must consent to cross-cloud data egress at purchase.

I’ll start drafting the co-sell enablement checklist once you confirm SKU IDs and region list.

Claire

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aws-partner.com>; sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood listing — initial SKU + region asks

Claire — quick commercial note: for co-sell tracking we’ll want a consistent offer ID per cloud so sales credits map correctly. Marissa, please confirm if RW-DED-BASE should be three separate offer IDs (one per cloud) or a single canonical offer with region tags. We prefer separate IDs to make marketplace incentives and quota simpler for partners.

Also attaching the canary playbook for internal review — this includes monitoring thresholds and rollback steps when fallback triggers.

Attachment: canary-fallback-playbook.pdf (internal)

Thanks,
Ben Carter | Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aws-partner.com>; rafael.gomez@azure-marketplace.com; priya.shah@gcp-partner.org
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai; jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing lift-and-fallback: SKU prioritization per cloud

Hi Claire / Rafael / Priya — thanks for the input. Final decisions from our side: 

1) SKU IDs (final): RW-API-STD, RW-DED-BASE-AWS, RW-DED-BASE-AZURE, RW-DED-BASE-GCP, RW-PRIV-VPC.
2) We will list Dedicated as three cloud-specific offers (separate offer IDs) to simplify co-sell attribution.
3) Day-one regions confirmed: AWS(us-east-1, us-west-2), Azure(East US, West US), GCP(us-central1). EU fallbacks are set but gated until capacity confirmation.
4) Canary: RW-API-CANARY will be a private offer with an allowlist (10 customers) and explicit consent for cross-cloud fallback to RW-API-STD.

I’ve uploaded the CSV and the canary playbook to the shared drive and added the HubSpot record HS-1234567. Next steps: Claire — can your ops team open the onboarding ticket once you have the CSV? Rafael/Priya — can you confirm any cloud-specific packaging fields we missed?

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Head, Cloud GTM — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_marketplace_sku_map_v1.csv; canary-fallback-playbook.pdf
